title: Renal Elimination

items.text: ●  Glomerular filtration: free (unbound) drug passes from blood into the renal tubule based on molecular size.

emphasis.text: ●  Glomerular filtration:

items.md: **●  Glomerular filtration:** free (unbound) drug passes from blood into the renal tubule based on molecular size.

items.text: ●  Tubular secretion: active transporters move additional drug from blood into the tubule.

emphasis.text: ●  Tubular secretion:

items.md: **●  Tubular secretion:** active transporters move additional drug from blood into the tubule.

items.text: ●  Tubular reabsorption: lipophilic, un-ionized drug can passively diffuse back into the blood, reducing net elimination.

emphasis.text: ●  Tubular reabsorption:

items.md: **●  Tubular reabsorption:** lipophilic, un-ionized drug can passively diffuse back into the blood, reducing net elimination.

notes: Urine pH manipulation (e.g., alkalinizing urine in aspirin overdose) works by trapping ionized drug in the tubule, blocking reabsorption.
